newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila court upholds ban on constitution change.
newsitem.headline: Manila court upholds ban on constitution change.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Tuesday upheld its ban on attempts to petition for a change in the constitution to allow President Fidel Ramos to run for a second term, a court source said.
The vote among the court members was a tie, which means its previous decision disallowing the petition stands, the source, who asked not to be identified, said.
Political analysts said the decision by the court to keep the ban virtually dashed the hopes of Ramos's supporters to keep him in office when his current six-year term expires next June.
"If it's a tie the rule is maintenance of the status quo," the source said, after the judges voted 6-6, with two abstentions, on whether to uphold its March ruling to ban the petition.

A citizens group launched the campaign to amend the constitution by collecting what it said was almost five million signatures to force the calling of a referendum on lifting the current term limits on incumbent officials.

Ramos has distanced himself from the group and repeatedly denied he has any plans of running for re-election in the May 1998 presidential polls. The 10-year-old constitution limits a president to only one term.
